notes: SHIP v1.14.391 - RACK FIRST-MOUNT LIFECYCLE + THREE VISUAL DEFECTS. Two specialist agents were run under the new execution directive; both returned FAIL with evidence, and every fix below traces to quoted code. ROOT CAUSE OF THE BLANK RACK, WITH IN-REPO PRECEDENT: showMode() disposes the Command hero WebGL context and then calls bw_render() SYNCHRONOUSLY in the same call stack, so the Build mount requests a new context microseconds after forceContextLoss(). Desktop Chrome always grants it; on iOS WebKit the GPU-side reclaim is asynchronous, the context is never granted, and three.js swallows the loss SILENTLY - a canvas exists and nothing draws, which is why nothing was ever logged or thrown. This is not a new theory: v1.14.342 already hit and fixed exactly this for the Command hero, its own comment reading "GPU contexts not yet free / page mid-layout", using a bounded re-arm. THAT FIX WAS NEVER PORTED TO BUILD. It is ported now - bw_mount3D re-arms up to 12 times at 400ms, the same 5-second budget as .342, and only then shows the terminal card. It also verifies a context was actually granted (getContext returns the SAME context three.js holds, not a second one) and treats lost-on-creation as a re-arm rather than a success. SECOND CODE-CERTAIN BUG, FIXED: nothing in this app listened for webglcontextlost anywhere - a repo-wide search found it only inside three.min.js - so any eviction after a good mount blanked the rack with no warning, no toast and no recovery. The Build canvas now listens and re-arms itself. THIRD CODE-CERTAIN BUG, FIXED: the zero-size retry inside the SHARED rackElevation_render3D decided retry-versus-bail by reading #reh3dCanvasHost, the rack-detail PANEL host, even when handed the Command hero or the Build mount; depending on session history that was either a bare console.warn bail or an UNCAPPED rAF spin against a mount the user had already left. The panel keeps its original condition, every other consumer is judged on its OWN mount, and the retry is bounded at 60 frames. THE SCENE IS UNTOUCHED - lighting, materials, geometry, fog, camera direction, floor, reflection, tone mapping, tray geometry and TYPE_COLORS are exactly as they were. Lifecycle only. VISUAL DEFECT 1, CRITICAL, AND IT WAS MINE: the desktop rule .bw-card:not(.bw-hero):not(.bw-prev) placed BOTH the Next Action card and the Worklist card into the same grid cell, because the worklist also carries .bw-card. Two cards rendered on top of each other and Next Action was unreadable at every laptop and desktop width. It shipped in .388 and was not caught because it produces no overflow - only a rect comparison finds it. Each now has its own named grid area. Measured before: identical rects. Measured after: Next Action at 932,206 and Worklist at 274,1357, no intersection. VISUAL DEFECT 2, HIGH, PRE-EXISTING: the phone header wordmark is a fixed 172px image sharing a flex row with the redesign-only tab, version and net pills, whose combined intrinsic width far exceeds any phone viewport - the wordmark overlapped the tab pill by about 93px at 390, 393 AND 430, and the COREWEAVE-SITE subtitle wrapped into three lines inside a 41px box. Nothing shrank because nothing was allowed to. Under body.rd at 480px and below the wordmark now caps at 118px and shrinks, the subtitle ellipsises to one line, and the tab-count pill stands down. The VERSION STAMP IS DELIBERATELY KEPT because it is what a device verify reads. ?legacy=1 keeps the header it ships with. VISUAL DEFECT 3: PORT MAP appeared twice in the same view, once as an action and again as a contextual tab. One door per feature is doctrine - the action was removed and the tab kept, leaving SCAN and LOG BLOCKER as a two-up row. VERIFIED BY INTERACTION, NOT BY READING: cold load to Command with a live hero context, then first open of Build - canvas present, no diagnostic; away to Command and back - canvas present; a real phase-completion re-render - canvas present; canvas count stable at 5 across all three, so no context leak. Phone header measured clean at 393. Desktop overlap measured gone at 1280. Zero horizontal overflow throughout. STILL OPEN AND HONESTLY DISCLOSED: the bottom nav fourth item is EXIT where the approved reference shows SHIFT; the rack-preview control rail wraps 4-then-1 and carries REAR and EXPLODE which the reference does not show; and the metrics render honest em-dashes because this harness rack has no Master-linked platform, so the metrics LAYOUT has not been visually verified against a populated rack. DEVICE-VERIFY: cold load, open Build, confirm the rack draws on the FIRST open; leave and return; complete a phase; confirm it draws every time. If it ever fails, the card now names the exact stop point.
